doc.title: Iola Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, CT, July 17, 2011

title: Worst gigs in Sweden and Finland
summary: Iola recalls a bare folkpark venue in Sweden with no audience, and Dave's similar Finland date with Mingus' group.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: I know one question I’ve tried a number of times and it hardly ever works is like what was your worst gig? And people tend not to — they’d have to really think about it.
Well there have been a few that stand out.
Well would the question work for you?

Well one that I can think of, it wasn’t that long ago, maybe in the 80s, and we were in Europe, and for some unknown reason the quartet was booked I guess it would be like in a folkpark or something, in, I think it was Sweden. And so we had a long drive from Stockholm to get to this place, and when we got there the venue was, it would be like maybe a rec room or something like that. It was just a low ceiling room. Nothing was set up. There were no speakers, no microphones, no nothing. And as it turned out, when it came time to perform, there were no people. I mean there was a handful of people there. And you go to all this effort.
You don’t expect that for the Dave Brubeck Quartet.

You just wonder why? Why? It didn’t make any sense at all. And then Dave tells about flying his group and Mingus’ group, flying to someplace in the North Pole as far as he’s concerned, in Finland, and a similar thing. When they got there they found the venue they were to play, it was in a classroom. And again, a handful of people. Why they were sent
there is beyond — a complete mystery. And no place for them to stay. So after they play, then they get back on a plane and fly back to Helsinki or someplace.
